# Routstr provider node — instructions for an operator's agent

Goal: help an operator set up a Routstr node without exposing the bootstrap admin password or assuming that a running API is a working provider. This file is a standalone entry point for agents without an existing checkout. The commands, Compose file and detailed human steps live in the checked-out repository; read `docs/provider/quickstart.md` and `docs/provider/deployment.md` after cloning.

## Boundaries

- Ask for approval of the target host, release tag, upstream type, public domain, spending limit, Nostr publication and payout settings before those actions. A local-only trial needs no domain or funded wallet.
- The operator enters admin passwords, upstream keys, Cashu credentials and Nostr secrets in their own trusted terminal/dashboard. Use an SSH tunnel to administer a remote private node. Never put secrets in chat, shell arguments, Git, captured logs or generated reports. A clean agent session may validate the workflow without seeing any credential.
- Keep setup private until the bootstrap password has been rotated. Never run bare `docker compose up`: stock `compose.yml` publishes port 8000 on all interfaces and starts Tor. Every Compose operation in this workflow uses `-f compose.node.yml`.
- Stop at a human authentication, funding or external-publication gate. Report the blocker, not a fabricated success.

## Workflow

1. Confirm Docker Compose and Python 3 on the chosen host, available disk and durable storage. Ask the operator to select a reviewed release tag; for testing the current development branch, explicitly label it as unreviewed. Clone `https://github.com/Routstr/routstr-core.git`, check out that ref, and inspect the quickstart and deployment guide before running commands. Reuse an existing checkout and state; do not overwrite `.env` or recreate a wallet.
2. Run `python3 scripts/node_setup.py start` from the checkout. It prepares a private `.env` only if missing, builds/starts `compose.node.yml`, waits for local info/models, and reports the private dashboard URL. On a remote host use `ssh -L 8000:127.0.0.1:8000 user@host` from the operator's machine. A private API with zero models is **not configured**.
3. Hand the operator the private dashboard address. Have them read the generated password privately from `docker compose -f compose.node.yml logs routstr`, log in, and immediately rotate it in Settings → Admin Settings. Do not ingest those logs into the agent context. Have them add the upstream in Providers, review pricing and payout settings, and enable at least one routable model.
4. Run `python3 scripts/node_setup.py check`. Require exit code 0 and a nonzero public model count. If it fails, diagnose without printing provider records or secrets. Do not call this a paid-inference test.
5. For production only, request approval for HTTPS publication and Nostr/analytics. Ensure a consistent, encrypted off-host backup of the database, secret key and wallet, with a tested isolated restore. Use a firewall and a reverse proxy to expose 443 while keeping port 8000 on loopback. Configure public URL and consented identity/relay settings. From a separate machine, run `python3 scripts/node_setup.py check --public-url https://node.example` and confirm expected identity and models.
6. With explicit approval of model, mint, prompt and spending limit, have the operator run small paid non-streaming and streaming inference tests with a funded client credential (not an admin token). Verify completion, accounting, upstream serving, refund status and payout separately. Do not claim production acceptance without these checks.

Handoff: report ref/version, private/public reachability, whether password rotation was confirmed (never the password), model count, backup/restore and paid-inference verification status, and remaining blockers. "Local API ready" and "production accepted" are separate outcomes. Never paste raw Docker logs or admin responses.
